item.title: Lakers announce final decision on Bronny James’ roster spot
item.description: Apr 26, 2026; Houston, Texas, USA; Los Angeles Lakers guard Bronny James (9) reacts after a play during the fourth quarter against the Houston Rockets during game four of the first round of the 2026 NBA Playoffs at Toyota Center. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers had a decision to make regarding their final roster spot ahead of Monday’s 5:00 PM Eastern deadline. Los Angeles final roster spot came down to draftmates Dalton Knecht and Bronny James, the son of Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James. Lakers head coach JJ Redick confirmed that the franchise would make its final decision ahead of the NBA’s deadline, and said that both players missed Monday’s practice due to feeling under the weather. Over the weekend, CBS Sports’ Sam Quinn asserted that the franchise should keep Knecht and trade James to a franchise that could be looking for help selling jerseys. “If I were the Lakers, I’d be trying to trade Bronny right now to some owner who wants to sell some jerseys,” Quinn posted on X. “I’d rather keep Knecht on the books as possible trade salary than cut him and deal with dead money. The Lakers don’t really need the James brand like other teams do.” “(He) Just hasn’t reached the point of offensive viability through two years,” Quinn added, “and the defensive threshold is just so freaking high at that size that if he’s never gonna make shots, he basically has to be a Jamal Shead-level pest to even justify a roster spot and he isn’t.” On Monday, as Redick promised, the franchise announced its final decision. “ The Los Angeles Lakers are waiving 2024 No. 17 pick Dalton Knecht, sources tell ESPN,” reported ESPN’s senior NBA Insider Shams Charania. The team changed. Needs changed, the fit changed. I think he’s gotten better as a player the last two years,” the coach siaid before Friday’s preseason finale. “I think, particularly last year, each guy got plenty of opportunities with the injuries we had. I just think coming into this year, we added a lot of wings,” Redick said at the time. “And he’s in a tough spot right now.” Only time will tell what James does with his opportunity, but he’s proven that he can make a roster without his father. item.title: Warriors' Steph Curry will play vs. Lakers Wednesday, but Golden State managing other injuries
item.description: Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry wears a Golden State Valkyries Veronica Burton jersey while warming up before a preseason game against the Portland Trail Blazers, Friday, Oct. 16, 2026, in San Francisco. (Jeff Chiu/Associated Press) The Bay Area can breathe a sigh of relief, for now. A day after Stephen Curry limped off the floor with a sprained ankle at Sunday's open practice, Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr told reporters that Curry will play in Wednesday's season opener against the Lakers. "I'm always concerned when Steph limps off," Kerr said Monday. "But I went down and checked on him, and he told me immediately he was fine." The sight brought audible shock to thousands at Chase Center Sunday, as Curry appeared to slip and roll his ankle before hobbling directly off the floor and straight to the locker room. Kerr, though, repeated after Sunday's practice that Curry was "fine," and said the Warriors star went through a full practice Monday. How much he'll actually play in Los Angeles Wednesday, now, is the question. Golden State has taken a specifically conservative approach to ramping Curry up this preseason after last year's knee troubles, as Kerr has previously indicated Curry could start the season playing below 32 minutes a game. The Warriors, too, may be shorthanded beyond Curry for Wednesday's opener. Guard Brandin Podziemski didn't practice Sunday or Monday with lower-back soreness, and Kerr termed him day-to-day. That could leave Golden State down a second starter against Los Angeles, as they already navigate the continued indefinite absence of center Kristaps Porzingis . There still has been no concrete timeline from Golden State for Porzingis's return after last week's remarkably public tweets making clear he's still working to recover from ongoing health issues. Kerr said the 31-year-old Porzingis won't travel with the Warriors to Los Angeles, and continued to emphasize his focus on Golden State's active roster when asked Monday about approaching communication with Porzingis. "I spoke to him a couple days ago," Kerr said. "We've texted, over the last couple of weeks. Other than my concern for him and his own well-being, I don't think of it – when we come to practice, I don't think of it, because I have to focus on the guys who are here. item.title: Milwaukee Bucks to waive Kevin Porter Jr.
item.description: The Milwaukee Bucks had until 4 p.m. CT on Oct. 19 to reduce its roster to, at maximum, 15 guaranteed contracts for the 2026-27 season, and to do so they will waive Kevin Porter Jr. Moving off the 26-year-old guard will create some minutes in a crowded back court for the Bucks as they begin the regular season in Washington D.C. on Oct. 21 . Porter had picked up his $5.3 million option in late June, but afterward the team acquired guards Tyler Herro and Kasparas Jakučionis in a trade with Miami, drafted guard Brayden Burries at No. 10 and re-signed Gary Trent Jr. in free agency. The Bucks also had guards Ryan Rollins and AJ Green under contract. Milwaukee Bucks guard/forward Kevin Porter Jr. (7) poses for a photo during Milwaukee Bucks media day at the Froedtert & MCW Sports Science Center in Milwaukee, Wisconsin on Sept. 28, 2026. HoopsHype, a USA TODAY NETWORK property, confirmed the Bucks' decision to waive Porter. Head coach Taylor Jenkins spoke to the media about an hour before that deadline after practice concluded. "It's another extremely difficult decision," he said of the impending move. "It's been a great process so far with [general manager] Jon [Horst]. The moment I got hired we were talking about these things. This isn't something that's just crept up the last couple weeks. It's been evaluating the entire group. "I think everyone, despite having depth in certain areas of our roster, everyone brings something different to the table and it's really trying to figure out what are the right pathways for us moving forward." The club re-signed Porter to a two-year deal in the 2025 offseason, and he played 38 games last season and dealt with a variety of injuries, which included two surgeries on his right knee. When healthy, he averaged 17.4 points, 7.4 assists and 5.2 rebounds per game last season. Originally drafted by the Bucks at No. 30 in 2019 and immediately traded to Cleveland, the Bucks reacquired Porter at the 2025 trade deadline in a deal with the Los Angeles Clippers for MarJon Beauchamp . In 68 games in Milwaukee (38 starts), Porter shot 42.8% overall, 36.1% from behind the 3-point line and averaged 14.9 points and 5.8 assists. "[Porter] is a very talented guy," Jenkins said. He's been great the last couple of weeks and just his approach, and I know he's hungry. He adds a lot to the table. He's a proven player in the league and excited to see what we ultimately do with this roster moving forward." item.title: Mario Cristobal doesn’t want to hear anyone talking about Miami (FL) being No. 1
item.description: Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Mario Cristobal doesn’t want to hear anyone talking about Miami (FL) being No. 1 appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Miami (FL) football is one of just six teams still undefeated this year. With losses from many of the top teams this week, such as Indiana and Notre Dame, Miami has moved up to the top spot in the AP Top 25 . Now, Mario Cristobal is talking about the ranking and what it means, per Ross Dellinger of Yahoo Sports. “The only way to play our butts off is to keep our mouths shut,” Cristobal said about being number one. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) It was not unanimous that Miami was the top team, and the top three teams are all very tight in the rankings. Miami ended up with 40 total first-place votes and 1697 points overall. Meanwhile, BYU took nine first-place votes and 1675 points overall. Ohio State had nine first-place votes and 1649 votes points overall. Texas Tech also received a first-place vote, but is ranked eighth overall. Miami has been receiving first-place votes nearly all season. They had one in the preseason poll, as well as one in Week 1, four in Week 2, one in Weeks 3 and 4, and two in Weeks 5 and 6. This week, they had 40 first-place votes, with 15 votes at second, 11 at third, one at fourth, two at fifth, and a single sixth-place vote. This is the first time since 2002 that Miami was ranked number one. They opened that season as the top-ranked team and held that ranking for the first ten weeks. Oklahoma jumped them in Week 11, but a loss to Texas A&M that week dropped them to fourth, and Miami took the top spot back. They held onto that spot until losing in double overtime to Ohio State in the BCS National Championship. Miami will put their top ranking on the line this Saturday at home as they host Pitt. item.description: Texas head coach Sean Miller coaches during Texas Basketball's final summer practice of the season in the Moody Center, Aug. 4, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) Texas basketball enters the season ranked No. 7 in the nation by The Associated Press , which marks the program's highest preseason ranking since the 2021-22 team began the year at No. 5. And second-year coach Sean Miller says bring on the hype . MORE: Texas Longhorns guard Mikey Lewis expected to return early, says Sean Miller "We signed up for high expectations," Miller told reporters Monday during a news conference on the University of Texas campus. "Why would you ever want to go to a program that has to trip over themselves to apologize about what they can't do, what they don't have, what they have to overcome? Why would you go there? At the University of Texas, we have that high-expectation environment. We have to embrace it, go for it, be about it, not run from it." Miller did his part to raise those expectations by following an 18-13 regular-season record a year ago with a run to the Sweet 16 in the NCAA Tournament. Miller and his staff then brought in 11 newcomers to the roster , including five transfers and six freshmen. Combined, those new players rank as the No. 1 overall class in the 2026 recruiting and portal cycle, according to 247 Sports . Texas has now made 22 appearances in school history in the AP preseason poll, including six of the last seven years. Eight of those preseason rankings have been in the top 10, including No. 6 in 1978-79, No. 4 in 2002-03, No. 2 in 2005-06, No. 7 in 2008-09, No. 3 in 2009-10, No. 10 in 2014-15, No. 5 in 2021-22 and this season. item.title: Former NC State coach Chuck Amato dies at 80 after memorable football career
item.description: Former NC State football coach Chuck Amato , who also spent years helping Bobby Bowden build Florida State into a national power, has died. He was 80. Amato died Monday after a recurrence of throat cancer. Amato was much more than a coach at NC State. He played linebacker for the Wolfpack from 1965-67 before returning to the school as an assistant coach. Years later, NC State hired him as its head coach, a job he held from 2000-06. Amato went 49-37 and took the Wolfpack to five bowl games. His biggest season came in 2002. With future NFL quarterback Philip Rivers leading the offense, NC State finished 11-3, beat Notre Dame in the Gator Bowl and finished No. 12 in the AP poll. The 11 wins remain the program’s single-season record. Amato also played an important role at Florida State. item.description: The Los Angeles Rams have another problem to address as they try to recover from a difficult start to the 2026 NFL season. Their latest defeat exposed continued concerns on special teams, leaving head coach Sean McVay with another decision to make. Los Angeles lost 20-19 to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday after a late field goal decided the contest. The Rams had hoped their latest roster move would provide greater stability after an inconsistent stretch from their previous kicker. Instead, the game brought another setback for a team already searching for answers. The Rams must now reassess their options as they prepare for Week 7 and attempt to steady a special teams unit that has struggled to find consistency. MORE: Mike McCarthy’s comments could change Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers’ role Blake Grupe tears ACL after injury against Cardinals Los Angeles Rams kicker Blake Grupe (19) Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The Rams’ latest setback involves kicker Blake Grupe, who tore his ACL during Sunday’s game against Arizona, according to Adam Schefter’s report. Los Angeles subsequently placed Grupe on injured reserve, ending his immediate return prospects after just one appearance with the team. Grupe suffered the knee injury while tackling Cardinals returner Devin Duvernay on a kickoff early in the game. The Rams had signed him from the New York Jets’ practice squad earlier in the week after moving on from Harrison Mevis. Rams kicker Blake Grupe tore his ACL. — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 19, 2026 Before the injury, Grupe had made a 44-yard field goal to give Los Angeles an early lead. However, he left for medical evaluation and did not return. His ACL tear now leaves the Rams needing another replacement at a position that has already brought them significant frustration this season. Rams must search for another kicker before Week 7 Grupe’s injury forces Los Angeles to revisit its kicking plans almost immediately. The team had brought him in hoping to improve its reliability after Mevis struggled in the previous game against Buffalo. Mevis had converted five of nine field-goal attempts before the Rams moved on from him. His misses included a blocked potential game-winner in the overtime loss to the Bills. Grupe’s arrival offered a fresh option, but his injury means the team must search for another solution. The Rams could explore free-agent kickers or make another move through the practice squad. They also need to settle their kicking operation quickly, since an injury to the specialist can affect extra points, field goals and kickoff responsibilities. At 2-4 entering the Cardinals matchup, Los Angeles has little margin for further mistakes. McVay’s team must stabilize its special teams while its offense works to produce more consistent results. item.title: Ben Crenshaw Fixes Putting With One Simple Move
item.description: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect Most golfers panic when their putter starts misbehaving. They immediately swap grips, buy new clubs, or try to rebuild their entire stroke from scratch. This approach usually makes things worse. Ben Crenshaw, a player with two Masters titles in 1984 and 1995, took a different path when his game went sideways. He kept his stroke constant and adjusted the ball position instead. According to MyGolfSpy , Crenshaw believed that changing the stroke is what gets people in trouble. His fix was imperceptible, moving the ball just a little up or back until the roll looked right. This subtle shift offers a solution for amateurs who struggle with consistency on the greens. The core of Crenshaw’s philosophy rests on repeatability. Putting is a personal game, and finding a stroke you can reproduce under pressure is vital. A new stroke you cannot repeat is not a fix; it creates a new problem. MyGolfSpy reports that Crenshaw’s approach holds the stroke constant while adjusting the variables around it. He noted that ball position isn’t just about forward and back movement. His swing suffered when he stood too far forward in his stance and approached the ball too closely. He described his stroke as freer than most, and a free-flowing stroke needs room to work. Diagnosing the Roll Identifying the right position requires watching how the ball leaves the face. MyGolfSpy outlines specific symptoms and the corresponding adjustments needed. If the ball skids or hops off the putter face, the player should try moving it slightly forward. Conversely, if putts pull to the left or launch high and bounce, moving the ball slightly back often corrects the issue. When the stroke feels cramped, the player needs to check their distance from the ball, not just the forward or backward alignment. Crenshaw’s answer was essentially to move the ball until the roll looks right. This honest approach relies on visual feedback rather than rigid rules. item.title: Lakers make Bronny James stance clear after waiving Dalton Knecht
item.description: The Los Angeles Lakers have made their decision on their roster for the 2026-27 NBA season. With a deadline approaching and one more player needing to go, the team had to choose between keeping its options open in a potential trade and making a cut. The decision carries different implications as the Lakers prepare to begin the regular season. Their final move also offers a glimpse into how the franchise is approaching its roster and development plans. MORE: Ben Simmons’ comeback derailed by devastating injury Lakers keep Bronny James after Dalton Knecht decision Los Angeles Lakers guard Bronny James. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images The Lakers’ decision to waive Knecht leaves James on the roster as Los Angeles prepares for the regular season. Both players had been discussed as potential options while the team worked through its roster crunch. James was selected 55th overall in the 2024 NBA Draft. The Lakers have continued to invest in his progress, and keeping him on the roster gives him another opportunity to develop within the team. The team chose to move on from Knecht, who had struggled to maintain a consistent role after showing promise during his rookie campaign. The Lakers entered the final roster decisions with 16 players on guaranteed standard contracts, leaving them one spot over the NBA’s 15-player limit. The team explored trade possibilities involving Knecht but did not find a deal before the deadline. Head coach JJ Redick had recently acknowledged that the team’s needs had changed and that increased competition among wing players had left Knecht in a difficult position. “I think the biggest thing is the team changed,” Redick said before the Lakers’ preseason finale. “The needs changed. The fit changed.” Knecht’s situation also followed a failed trade involving center Mark Williams. The Lakers had briefly dealt Knecht to the Charlotte Hornets as part of that transaction, but the deal fell through and he returned to Los Angeles. The Lakers can turn their attention to the regular season. item.title: Man United make contact for Felix Nmecha ahead of January, Dortmund lay down their conditions
item.description: Man United make contact for Felix Nmecha ahead of January, Dortmund lay down their conditions Manchester United remain keen to further reinforce their midfield in upcoming transfer windows. Jason Wilcox, the club’s director of football, prioritised the midfield over all other squad issues during the summer as he sought to revamp United’s options, signing Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba. Baleba has impressed in his first three appearances, but Santos and Tielemans have produced mixed performances so far and have left a lot to be desired. Manchester United “ready to battle” Liverpool for Felix Nmecha According to TEAMtalk , Manchester United are considering a move for Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha . It is claimed that United, who were strongly linked with Nmecha over the summer, have maintained a persistent interest in the Germany international and are understood to have “made contact as they assess options ahead of the winter window.” Nmecha came through the ranks at Manchester City before establishing himself at Wolfsburg and then Borussia Dortmund in Germany. It is believed that the 26-year-old’s background adds to his appeal in England. “His performances for club and country have strengthened his reputation as a versatile, energetic central midfielder capable of contributing in both boxes,” the report adds. Apart from United, Liverpool are also thought to be keen on Nmecha. Dortmund remain firm Nmecha extended his contract until June 2030 earlier this year and is considered central to head coach Niko Kovač’s plans. Furthermore, there is no active release clause that can be triggered in January, with sources indicating that an €80 million (£67.4m) clause will become available only from the summer of 2027. Meanwhile, Dortmund allegedly value him significantly higher, with figures in the region of €90-100m frequently mentioned. As such, it would be difficult to sign Nmecha from Dortmund mid-season, and “any realistic move is more likely to materialise at the end of the season, not in the coming weeks.” The Peoples Person Reliability Assessment Overall credibility: 5/10 Why? ✅ Interest in midfielder widely reported in the summer ✅ The player’s profile suited to Premier League football ⚠️ Source has a poor track record TPP view We believe Nmecha has the skill set to improve United, but the suggestion of a move seems far-fetched.

item.title: Real Madrid star ‘considering his future’ amid Premier League interest
item.description: Real Madrid star ‘considering his future’ amid Premier League interest Real Madrid star Trent Alexander-Arnold is taking into consideration a potential move away from the club in 2027. item.title: Ronaldo given 30-day suspension and £215 fine by Portuguese FA
item.description: Ronaldo has scored 146 goals in 234 Portugal appearances [Getty Images] Cristiano Ronaldo has been given a 30-day suspension and fined 255 euros (£215) by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) after leaving his country's international camp last month. The 41-year-old captain walked out of Portugal's Nations League squad in September after being an unused substitute against Norway and then finding out he would not start against Denmark on 1 October. Ronaldo said in a lengthy statement he had left because Portugal coach Jorge Jesus twice "broke his word", accusing him of an "absolute breach of trust". The Al-Nassr forward's suspension takes effect from the day of the Denmark match, meaning he has already served 19 days of his ban and will not miss any Portugal matches. Portugal face Denmark in the Nations League again on 14 November before travelling to Wales three days later. The FPF disciplinary committee said it took into account "the remorse shown" by Ronaldo in his statement, as well as his "contributions to soccer and recognition for athletic merit". It added that the forward submitted his CV, including his awards and achievements, as part of his defence. Ronaldo also referred the committee to his earlier statement, where he accepted accountability and apologised to his team-mates and fans for his actions, before adding he deserved to be punished. Portugal boss Jesus denied making any agreement with Ronaldo but has left the door open for his return. Pedro Proenca, president of the FPF, told Portuguese outlet Record there is a "strong desire" to have Ronaldo back with the national team once the matter is resolved. The five-time Ballon d'Or winner has scored 146 goals in 234 Portugal appearances - both men's world records - helping them win Euro 2016 and the two Nations League titles. He joined Saudi Arabian side Al-Nassr in December 2022 on a reported annual salary of £177m and signed a contract extension last year. item.title: Boomer Esiason concerned NFL game could inspire rioters in Paris
item.description: Credit: CBS Sports Network Despite nationwide protests, the NFL is moving forward with its scheduled game between the New Orleans Saints and Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris. And Boomer Esiason has concerns. The NFL’s International Series continues Sunday, with the Saints and Steelers playing at Stade de France . The game will take place amid civil unrest in France stemming from student-led protests over poor school conditions, which have escalated into widespread anti-government demonstrations and some riots. On Monday morning, a WFAN caller asked Esiason and co-host Gregg Giannotti why NFL commissioner Roger Goodell chose to move forward with the game in Paris despite the civil unrest in France. While the NFL claims there is no concern about the area hosting the game, Esiason wonders whether the game might attract social unrest. “If you want to amplify your unrest, the best way to do it would be around an NFL football game in France.” – Boomer Esiason https://t.co/9MT3ZYWFRz — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) October 19, 2026 “They claim where they are going that there is no unrest,” Esiason said. “But if you want to amplify your unrest, the best way to do it would be around an NFL football game in France. It is ugly over there right now, and it’s basically uncontrolled… I don’t necessarily know that the French government has the stones to put it to rest. item.title: Steelers’ Mike McCarthy defends play-calling after Jamel Dean interception
item.description: (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers mounted their biggest fourth-quarter comeback in over 30 years on Sunday by overcoming a 16-3 deficit to defeat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. One of the biggest plays of the game came when former Buccaneer Jamel Dean picked off Jalon Daniels and returned the interception inside the five yard-line. Unfortunately for Pittsburgh, they were unable to punch the ball in the end zone. The first play on the ensuing drive was a play action pass intended for Darnell Washington that was broken up. The second play was a run by Jaylen Warren that put the ball to the one yard-line. Then on 3rd-and-goal, Aaron Rodgers threw a jump ball to DK Metcalf that was broken up, which lead to the Steelers kicking a field goal. Many were critical of the play-calling from Mike McCarthy, but the Steelers’ head coach defended his choice of plays on Monday. “I get the post evaluation, but those are solid plays,” McCarthy said. The Steelers were able to overcome not getting into the end zone late in the fourth quarter. Despite the Bucs getting into field goal range and sending the game into overtime, the Steelers drove 12 plays and Rodgers connected with Germie Bernard for the game-winning score. item.description: Photo by David Cannon/Getty Images Jordan Spieth once insisted that he had an awesome relationship with Patrick Reed despite the infamous press conference following the 2018 Ryder Cup in France. Spieth and Reed once looked destined to become Team USA’s greatest ever pairing in the Ryder Cup. They won two and went unbeaten during their three matches together at Gleneagles in 2014. And in 2016, they delivered 2.5 points from their four matches at Hazeltine. Reed went on to produce a stunning performance in the singles to defeat Rory McIlroy. They were also dominant at the Presidents Cup the following year. So it would have come as a surprise to many when Jim Furyk opted to not put the two men together during the 2018 Ryder Cup at Le Golf National. Jordan Spieth commented on the decision to split him and Patrick Reed up at the 2018 Ryder Cup Spieth played in all four sessions with Justin Thomas , while Reed featured twice over the first two days alongside Tiger Woods . With the Americans suffering a heavy defeat, questions were asked about not pairing Spieth and Reed together. Reed subsequently claimed that Spieth had decided that he did not want to play with him. He was critical of how Furyk handled the situation. However, Spieth went on to explain to Subpar in 2020 that there was no lingering ill-feeling between himself and the 2018 Masters champion. “It was 2015 in the Presidents Cup in Korea, and Jay Haas was the captain. He came to me and was like, ‘hey, who do you want to play with this week?’ Which is kind of a cool position to be in. He’s like, ‘you’re leading our team, who do you want to play with?’ I was like, ‘well, I want to play with Patrick, we’ve had success last year at the Ryder Cup. I’d love to play a round with DJ [Dustin Johnson], I think that would be so much fun’. I’ve actually battled with DJ more than I have anybody else on the PGA Tour, whether it’s majors or PGA Tour events, and I’ve loved it. I’ve played more groups in his group than I have anyone else. He’s like, ‘you’re leading our team, who do you want to play with?’ I was like, ‘well, I want to play with Patrick, we’ve had success last year at the Ryder Cup. I’d love to play a round with DJ [Dustin Johnson], I think that would be so much fun’. I’ve actually battled with DJ more than I have anybody else on the PGA Tour, whether it’s majors or PGA Tour events, and I’ve loved it. I’ve played more groups in his group than I have anyone else. So I was like, ‘I want to play with DJ, this would be awesome. I’d love playing from his drives, this would be great. And then he’s going to have to play from mine. He’s going to be like I don’t really want to hit seven iron’,” he said. “I had already played with DJ, and then played with Patrick later in the week. He made a birdie, he came over and he’s like, ‘that’s what you get for playing with DJ’. I was like, ‘we both made eight birdies through 14 holes and destroyed whoever we were playing’. It was almost like I’d fired him up more, playing with somebody else. “But I grew up with Justin. He’s one of my best friends in the entire world. Since we were 13, we’ve been the biggest fans of each other through our entire process of junior golf, college golf, professional golf, into winning major championships, being number one in the world. We’ve accomplished these massive goals we set out when we were 13 at Mansfield, we were paired there and that’s where we met. So obviously I want to play with him. This would be so awesome. “The team room, it was fine. We all had people we were going to play with. When we were getting ready for the tournament, I think it was myself, Tiger, Justin, and Patrick, which was freaking badass to play in a pod with Tiger at the Ryder Cup. You might be paired with him, even though we knew he was going to be Justin’s partner if I played with Patrick, and then Patrick and Tiger might play together. I also didn’t think it would be a big deal if I played with Justin, and Patrick got Tiger. It doesn’t seem like something that would upset people, that you get Tiger. It was part of the pod. “For me, we had grown up together, we had accomplished these goals together, we’re finally at the coolest stage in golf, the Ryder Cup, let’s go out and kick some ass together. That’s what we wanted to do. Everyone was fine, nothing was a big deal. Things were raised afterwards, and then Patrick and I have been awesome since. It really was blown out for six months, and then other than that, it’s been nothing.” Jim Furyk will have learnt plenty from his management of Patrick Reed at Le Golf National While Furyk made some big mistakes with Reed, it is difficult to make the case that he was wrong to put Spieth and Thomas together in Paris. They won three points from four matches together, with Thomas ending the week alongside Tommy Fleetwood as the second highest points scorer across the two teams. Brooks Koepka was the only American player who came close to matching Reed’s win rate of nearly 78 per cent leading into that week. So pairing Reed with Woods, who would have inevitably been exhausted following his Tour Championship victory the previous week, was an error. It was not Furyk’s biggest misstep. Few will forget Phil Mickelson and Bryson DeChambeau being sent out together in foursomes. But it is certainly one of the mistakes Furyk will have on his mind as he looks to secure a better result in 2027.

item.description: European governing body gives two-week deadline Letter addresses other issues including Balogun affair Uefa has given Fifa a two-week deadline to release key documents relating to Gianni Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan and other governance issues in its latest critique of football’s world governing body . A letter sent to Fifa’s general secretary, Mattias Grafström, by his counterpart at Uefa, Theodore Theodoridis, is accompanied by an eight-page document that has more than 50 questions about Fifa’s handling of dozens of issues over the past 12 months. These include the proposed sale of 20% of its commercial rights, the Folarin Balogun affair , the peace prize and relations with Donald Trump and the arrangements for next year’s Fifa presidential election. Uefa’s document also makes a number of allegations about potential conflicts of interests at Fifa, as well as repeating calls for a “genuinely independent” governance review. Continue reading...

The sporting director, Max Eberl, who stood in for his coach in the post-match press conference, explained that the Belgian had been ill, not to mention Kompany’s current hip problem that had made the move from dressing room to pitchside slow and uncomfortable. item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Watford, a ‘fake news’ sacking and an apology to Elton John
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.description: It’s not just that the club’s recent charges themselves are unprecedented – it’s the language used to describe them too Sign up for our free newsletter here The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: Mikel Arteta’s new contract reflects where the power now lies at Arsenal | Ed Aarons
item.description: From transfers to stadium works and even the training-ground dog, there is no doubting the Spaniard’s influence at the club If anyone doubts Mikel Arteta’s status as No 1 at Arsenal in the week he committed his future to the club until 2030 , just ask Win the dog. The chocolate labrador who played a starring role in the celebrations when Arsenal were crowned Premier League champions in May has become part of the family at the training ground in Hertfordshire since being introduced by Arteta in May 2023. Kai Havertz, David Raya and Mikel Merino, who issues commands in Spanish and has spoken about spending time with Win when out for three months with a foot injury, are particular favourites. But, according to sources close to Win, a therapy dog trained not to bark, there is no contest when it comes to her preferred human: Arteta. Continue reading...

item.title: Lionel Messi’s Argentina career turned football into a sacred mystery
item.description: Jorge Messi wanted his country to fall in love with his son. That ambition was fulfilled during a brilliant international career that ended this week “What Argentina is doing in this World Cup is of a sacred order,” Brazilian writer Milly Lacombe posted at the height of the tide of anti-Argentinian sentiment during this year’s tournament. She was exploring the contradiction she felt around her support of Lionel Messi: “a player who is a God and a man who shakes Trump’s hand”. Lacombe highlighted the importance of acknowledging the complexities around Messi and the Argentinian team. How is it possible that Messi was not speaking out against the racist incidents we all saw around the Argentina team , she asked. “That’s why it hurts so much to see someone with Messi’s power choosing to make himself small,” she wrote. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
